# Importing Data {#sec-import-dataset-dlg}

The **Import Dataset** dialog controls how a data file is read into a project.
To open it, click the `r keys("Add")` button in the **Datasets** section of the **Data** tab.

To change how an existing dataset is imported, select the dataset and click the `r keys("Edit Import")` button in the same section.
This opens the same dialog (titled **Edit Import Settings**) with the dataset's current settings.

The dialog shows a preview of the data that updates as you change its options.

## File {-}

**Filepath**: Shows the path of the file being imported.

**Change File...**: Click this button to import a different data file.

**Refresh from file**: Click this button to re-read the columns from the file.
(Your current settings are kept.)
This is useful if the file has changed since the dialog was opened.

## Options {-}

**Worksheet**: Select the worksheet to import.
This option is only shown for *Excel* (`.xlsx`) and *OpenDocument* (`.ods`) spreadsheets.

**Skip rows**: Enter the number of rows to skip before reading the data.
This is useful for files that have notes or titles above the column headers.

**Max discrete value**: Enter the largest integer that a column can contain and still be seen as discrete (i.e., categorical).
When the program deduces a column's data type, a column with an integer larger than this value is classified as continuous.
For example, a column of survey responses coded 1–5 would be seen as categorical, while a column of ages would be seen as continuous.
The default value is 7.

**Leading zeros as text**: Check this option to import numeric columns with leading zeros as text.
This is useful for fixed-width numeric IDs (e.g., *00451*) that are labels, rather than continuous values.

**Years as text**: Check this option to import columns of four-digit numbers as text.
These numbers are assumed to be years.

**Sort column names (grouped by type)**: Check this option to sort the column names alphabetically after importing.
The columns are grouped by their data type.

**Missing data codes (comma separated)**: Enter the values that should be treated as missing data, separated by commas (e.g., *NA, N/A, NULL*).
Empty cells are always treated as missing data.

**ID column**: Select the column that identifies each row (e.g., a student or employee ID).
Select **(None)** if the data does not have an ID column.

## Column Data Types {-}

**Column data type**: Select a column in the preview grid, then select its data type from this list.
The program deduces each column's type when the file is read, but you can override it here.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Data types
:::

**Text**: The column is imported as categorical text.

**Categorical**: The column is imported as integer codes that represent categories (e.g., *1* = *Agree*).

**Numeric**: The column is imported as continuous values (i.e., floating-point numbers or a wide range of integers).

**Date**: The column is imported as dates.

**Do not import**: The column is left out of the dataset.
::::

## Preview {-}

The preview grid shows the data as it will be imported with the current settings.
Columns that will not be imported are shown in a different style.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
The preview only shows the first 300 rows of the file.
All rows are imported when you click `r keys("OK")`.
:::
